title: Growing Together · Early Learning Curriculum
ageScope: Birth through age six; final pathway covers 5- and 6-year-olds (60–83 months).
approach: Play-based, whole-child, responsive and inclusive, with intentional teaching and inquiry as useful.

areas.title: Relationships & regulation
areas.goal: Warm relationships, co-regulation, belonging, turn taking and solving social problems.
areas.frameworkConnection: Social and Emotional Development; Approaches to Learning

areas.title: Communication & early literacy
areas.goal: Back-and-forth communication, home languages, stories, sound awareness, reading and purposeful writing.
areas.frameworkConnection: Language and Communication / Language and Literacy; Approaches to Learning

areas.title: Movement & self-care
areas.goal: Safe movement, coordination, body awareness, participation in daily care and growing practical independence.

areas.title: Thinking & mathematics
areas.goal: Attention, memory, comparison, spatial thinking, number relationships and flexible problem solving.
areas.frameworkConnection: Cognition / Mathematics Development; Approaches to Learning

areas.title: Science & inquiry
areas.goal: Close observation, questions, cause and effect, living things and testing ideas safely.
areas.frameworkConnection: Cognition / Scientific Reasoning; Approaches to Learning

areas.title: Creative expression
areas.goal: Original choices through art, music, movement, construction and representation.
areas.frameworkConnection: Integrated expression across domains; Approaches to Learning

areas.title: Community & belonging
areas.goal: Family identity, home cultures, access, respectful relationships and care for shared places.
areas.frameworkConnection: Social and Emotional Development; Language and Communication

ageBands.title: Young infants
ageBands.label: Birth–5 months
ageBands.organization: Individual, cue-based interactions during care and brief comfortable awake play.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Notice cues → respond warmly → pause for a response → adjust or stop.
ageBands.priority: Secure relationships and access to everyday experience; no academic drills or group-performance goals.

ageBands.title: Older infants
ageBands.label: 6–11 months
ageBands.organization: Safe floor exploration with a nearby responsive adult; repeated familiar experiences.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Follow interest → offer a safe object/action → wait → acknowledge the child’s response.
ageBands.priority: Support emerging mobility and communication without forcing positions or milestones.

ageBands.title: Young toddlers
ageBands.label: 12–23 months
ageBands.organization: Predictable routines, concrete materials, movement and short shared play.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Offer a choice → show one useful action → allow repetition → support a transition.
ageBands.priority: Use real objects and home-language words; emerging skills need adult support.

ageBands.title: Older toddlers
ageBands.label: 24–35 months
ageBands.organization: Parallel play, pretend routines, simple problem solving and supported peer encounters.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Prepare two or more accessible choices → join briefly → model language → step back.
ageBands.priority: Participation and regulation vary widely; no forced sharing or required sitting.

ageBands.title: Preschool
ageBands.label: 3 years · 36–47 months
ageBands.organization: Longer self-chosen center play with brief optional guided invitations and rich conversation.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Notice an idea → add a question or material → support a test or representation → revisit.
ageBands.priority: Build concepts through play, movement, stories and relationships; avoid worksheets as the core.

ageBands.title: Pre-K
ageBands.label: 4 years · 48–59 months
ageBands.organization: Sustained play and projects with intentional small-group language, literacy and math.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Connect to experience → model a strategy → invite use → reflect with evidence.
ageBands.priority: Offer explicit teaching within meaningful work; do not make a birthday a readiness rule.

ageBands.title: Kindergarten bridge
ageBands.label: 5- and 6-year-olds · 60–83 months
ageBands.organization: Play, purposeful projects and accessible explicit instruction, coordinated with the child’s school.
ageBands.teachingCycle: Choose a meaningful purpose → teach a needed tool → apply it → discuss and revise.
ageBands.priority: Includes children through age six. This author-designed bridge is not a verified state kindergarten curriculum.

lessons.title: Notice a cue, answer, and pause
lessons.materials: Attentive familiar caregiver; quiet comfortable space
lessons.aim: Build trust through a predictable response to an infant’s communication.
lessons.readiness: Use the pathway as a starting point, not a test. Look for interest and comfortable access; offer a simpler or more complex version as needed.
steps: Observe a small movement, sound, facial change or turning away.
Respond with a gentle voice or appropriate care, then pause.
Notice the next cue and adjust rather than continuing automatically.
lessons.interest: Build trust through a predictable response to an infant’s communication.
lessons.control: The child’s actions, communication and the real result provide feedback. The adult checks safety and meaning, models as needed, and does not require a correct performance.
lessons.observe: What cue occurred, the adult response and whether the infant settled, engaged or needed something else.
lessons.nextStep: Repeat the response pattern during a familiar routine.
lessons.safety: Follow the infant’s individual care plan and safe positioning. Never withhold feeding, comfort or needed care to create a learning trial.
lessons.adaptations: Offer home-language words, signs, visual cues, stable positioning and adapted materials as useful. Participation can be watching, touching, moving, pointing or another comfortable response.
lessons.familyConnection: Share one factual observation and ask what the family notices or enjoys at home. Suggest an optional everyday version using safe familiar materials; no purchase or homework is expected.
